text:
**For a full recharge in one day, plan on roughly 300-350 W of solar. If you can wait a day and a half or so, 200 W is enough.**

**The formula:** panel watts ≈ 1,000 Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 factor covers real-world losses from heat, panel angle, and the charge controller. Panels rarely deliver their rated watts. ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge))

| Conditions | Peak sun hours | Panel watts for a 1-day recharge |
|---|---|---|
| Good summer | 5 | ~270-300 W |
| Typical | 4 | ~340 W |
| Northern winter | 2 | ~735 W |

Sources: [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/) and [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/).

- **Smaller panel:** A 200 W panel adds about 600-630 Wh on an average day, so it refills 1,000 Wh in about 1.5-2 days. ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station))
- **Peak sun hours:** These aren't daylight hours. Most of the US gets about 3-6 a day. Plan around your worst month, not the average. ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/))
- **Your station's solar input limit:** Panels above that limit add nothing. Many 1,000 Wh units accept 400-800 W, but cheaper ones cap at 200 W or less. ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/))
- **Voltage range:** Check your station's input voltage window, often around 12-60 V. Too high can damage it, and too low won't charge. ([SolarNiverse](https://solarniverse.com/chargers/charge-power-station-with-solar-panels/))

**One option:** If your station accepts 400 W and 12-60 V, the [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W Foldable Solar Panel](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) fits. At 4 peak sun hours it should deliver about 1,200 Wh a day, which is enough for a one-day refill.
- **Price:** The listing says $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26 (expires 2026-12-30). Checkout has the final word.
- **Specs:** Voc is 45.3 V, so it won't suit stations with low voltage limits. It weighs 18.5 kg (about 41 lb), which is heavy for a folding panel.
